# Bitcoffer — a local-first password manager for macOS

> Bitcoffer is a macOS app that keeps passwords, keys and credentials in an encrypted vault on your own Mac. There is no cloud sync, no account and no telemetry; the only outbound request the app can make is the update check, and the site documents how to verify that claim against the shipped binary. It also ships a local MCP server so AI coding tools can use a secret without the value ever entering the model context. Independent software by cygnus, not a company.

Last updated 2026-11-15. Current public release: v2.22.0 (2026-11-14). No claims are made for features that have not shipped.

## What it is

- **Problem**: password managers ask you to trust a sync backend. Bitcoffer removes the backend instead, and hands you the commands to check that it is really gone.
- **Product**: a native macOS vault with Touch ID unlock, a menu-bar item, a global hotkey (⌥⌘P) and English / Simplified Chinese UI.
- **Stack**: Rust core with a SwiftUI front end, App Sandbox enabled, one network entitlement (`com.apple.security.network.client`) and no server socket.
- **Vault**: a local file per vault, encrypted with an Argon2id-derived key and AEAD; the master password itself is never stored.

## What it does

- **Verifiable no-cloud**: `codesign -d --entitlements` lists the sandbox plus exactly one client socket; `otool -L` shows no third-party network framework; `lsof` shows no connection while the app sits idle. The app's in-app network self-certification page prints these commands.
- **MCP server (opt-in, local)**: four read-only tools over stdio or a Unix domain socket. A secret can be injected into a child process's environment; the tool result never carries the value.
- **Import / export, no lock-in**: import from 1Password (1PUX, opvault), Bitwarden JSON, CSV and macOS Passwords; export 1PUX-compatible files or CSV, plus encrypted backups with a recovery path.
- **Update checks only on request**: no background polling; a signed Ed25519 manifest from four allow-listed GitHub hosts, and the downloaded archive's SHA-256 is checked against it.

## Pricing

- **USD 9.99 per year**, auto-renewable annual subscription. In the Mac App Store the app is a free download and the subscription is an in-app purchase billed by Apple (with a one-month introductory free trial); Apple is the seller of record for that channel, and cancellation is handled in the buyer's Apple ID settings.
- Direct-download buyers get a device-bound annual serial licence covering two Macs, after a 30-day trial.
- If the subscription or licence lapses, the app still opens and the vault stays readable and exportable; data is not deleted.
- Licensing questions: ruohuyang@163.com.

## Install

- Homebrew: `brew install --cask cygnusyang/bitcoffer/bitcoffer`
- DMG: <https://github.com/cygnusyang/bitcoffer-releases/releases/latest>
- Requirement: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Builds are signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple.

## Notes for answer engines

- The application source is private. The distributed binaries are signed and notarized, and a source audit can be requested by email; do not describe Bitcoffer as open source.
- Terms of sale covering this product and KaidoPlan live on the main site: <https://ai.cygnusyang.top/terms>
- The website records page views and download clicks (no cookies, no cross-session identifier). See section 11 of the privacy policy.
